brand.title: ESourceAIG (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — ESource Team: How to Activate a New Accounting Firm

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the License Service in the ESource system?
choices: To store all client names and bank statements securely
To send sign-in codes, enforce plan limits, and hand out keys to unlock firm books
To manage the firm's branding and logo files
To process monthly billing payments from client firms
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right! The License Service is the backend that manages authentication, plan enforcement, and book access without ever seeing sensitive client data.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Not quite. The License Service never receives client names or bank statements—it focuses on authentication, plan limits, and access control instead.

questions.question: What four things must be in place before you can activate a firm?
choices: A signed agreement, agreed tier and book limit, security plan and lead named, and firm details collected
A signed agreement, the firm's accounting records, a Firm ID, and a web address
Pricing tiers confirmed, the admin page set up, brand colors chosen, and staff members hired
The firm's legal name, logo file, Vercel account, and a backup plan document
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect! These four prerequisites ensure the legal, technical, and security foundations are solid before activation begins.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Not quite. The four things are the signed agreement, the tier and book limit agreement, the security plan with a named lead, and the firm's details like name, logo, color, web address, and owner info.

questions.question: What is a Firm ID and why must it be chosen carefully?
choices: The firm's web address, which can be changed anytime to match rebranding
A short, lowercase identifier with no spaces that never changes once set
The name of the firm's owner, used only for internal record-keeping
A numeric code assigned by the License Service for billing purposes
questions.feedback_correct: Correct! The Firm ID is permanent, so picking a good one at the start saves headaches later.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Not quite. The Firm ID is a short, lowercase identifier with no spaces—like 'smithco'—and it's permanent, so it must be chosen with care during step one.

questions.question: In the profiles.js file, what does the 'firm' setting control?
choices: The firm's legal name used for tax filings and contracts
The name the firm's clients see on statement requests and Excel reports
The internal Firm ID that links to the admin page
The storage location where client books are encrypted and saved
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly! The 'firm' setting is the client-facing name, like 'Smith and Company' on their reports and statements.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Not quite. The 'firm' setting in profiles.js controls what clients see—it appears on statement requests and every page of the Excel reports.

questions.question: When setting up a domain in Vercel and Cloudflare, why is it important to set the proxy cloud to gray?
choices: Because a gray cloud encrypts all data traffic between the firm and ESource servers
Because it reduces the monthly cost of using Vercel's hosting platform
Because an orange cloud blocks Vercel's security certificate from working properly
Because it allows ESource to monitor the firm's usage without the firm knowing
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right! The gray cloud means DNS only, which allows Vercel's security certificate to function. An orange cloud would break it.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Not quite. Setting the proxy to gray (DNS only) is critical because an orange cloud blocks Vercel's security certificate. The correct setting ensures the firm's connection is secure.

questions.question: What is the first action the owner must take after signing in for the first time?
choices: Change their password and set up two-factor authentication
Add each staff member's name and work email on the License tab
Upload the firm's first client book and configure backup settings
Review the Help tab and enable reminders for monthly billing
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect! Adding staff members to the License tab is the first step because only people on that list can sign in.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Not quite. After the owner's first sign-in, their main task is to add staff members' names and emails to the License tab—this controls who can access the system.

questions.question: How is the help assistant configured differently for firms using their own domain versus an esourcebookkeeper.com domain?
choices: Firms using their own domain must disable the help assistant entirely for security
Firms using their own domain need to add that domain to the assistant's allowed websites in ElevenLabs
The help assistant works identically for both; no configuration difference is needed
Firms using their own domain must pay extra to access the help assistant feature
questions.feedback_correct: Correct! If the firm uses its own web address, you must add it to the assistant's allowed websites in ElevenLabs so the help button works.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Not quite. The help assistant works automatically on esourcebookkeeper.com subdomains, but if a firm uses its own domain, that domain must be added to the assistant's allowed websites in ElevenLabs.

questions.question: According to the billing model, how much should you bill a firm that had 15 client books active at peak usage this month?
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly! The first book is $20, and books 2–10 are $17 each. So: $20 + (14 × $17) = $258.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Not quite. The billing tiers are: $20 for book 1, then $17 for books 2–10, $15 for books 11–30, $14 for books 31–100, and $13 after that. For 15 books: $20 + (14 × $17) = $258.

questions.question: A firm's staff member's laptop goes offline and stays offline for 16 days without internet. What happens next?
choices: The books on that laptop are permanently deleted to prevent data loss
The laptop locks for safety, and the user must simply connect and sign in again to regain access
The License Service automatically notifies the firm's owner to replace the laptop
The user loses access permanently and must be removed from the License tab
questions.feedback_correct: Correct! Laptops lock after 14 days offline as a safety measure, but the fix is simple: reconnect and sign in.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Not quite. Computers lock after 14 days without internet for safety, but this isn't permanent—the user simply connects to the internet and signs in again to unlock their books.

questions.question: Why is it significant that the 'Ever added' count never goes down, even when a client book is deleted?
choices: Because it protects against fraud by keeping a permanent audit trail
Because it means you should consider offering the next tier if a firm frequently adds and deletes books
Because the firm will be billed for the total ever added, not just current active books
Because deleted books are actually not removed but hidden to prevent accidental recovery
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right! The 'Ever added' count is used for billing, so deleting and re-adding books repeatedly to avoid tier upgrades won't work.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Not quite. The 'Ever added' count never decreases, which means the firm is billed based on this total. This prevents someone from gaming the system by repeatedly deleting and re-adding the same books to stay in a lower tier.
